children: Contemplating the emerging triumph of free-market liberalism in his country, a Russian scholar is said to have quipped, “The future is clear and well-known. Only the past is worth studying, because only the past still has mystery.” The successes of corporate consolidation, free-ranging finance, and transnational economic standardization backed by military muscle have made it difficult for people all over the world to think beyond the story of neoliberal globalization. This story is not enough. Like the apocryphal Russian scholar, this book has turned away from the sureties of a self-making future to re-open a sense of mystery that might yet enrich the possibilities for imagining the about-to-be-present.
据说一位俄罗斯学者在思考自由市场自由主义在其国家新兴的胜利时打趣道：“未来是清楚而众所周知的。只有过去值得研究，因为只有过去仍有神秘。”企业整合、自由流动的金融以及军事力量支持的跨国经济标准化的成功，使世界各地的人们难以想象新自由主义全球化故事之外的东西。这个故事还不够。像那位轶闻中的俄罗斯学者，本书背离了自我制造未来的确定性，重新打开一种神秘感，它或许仍能丰富想象即将到来的当下的可能性。

How shall we re-open mystery in our times? To emerge from under the shadow of inevitability, it seems important to bring back the passions and the stakes of global connection. Instead of inscribing structures of self-fulfillment, we might immerse ourselves in the drama of uncertainty of global capitalism and transnational liberalism. What seems at first to be a minor skirmish may yet determine history. Since we don’t know how things will turn out, it’s worth attending to states of emergence—and emergency. Here hope and despair huddle together, sometimes dependent on the same technologies. Urgency springs up in ruined landscapes; utopian dreams, and crass ambitions, are formed. The guaranteed futures of globalization theory seem strange and far away in this storm.

我们如何重新打开时代的神秘？要走出必然性的阴影，似乎重要的是带回全球联结的激情与利害。与其铭刻自我实现的结构，我们不如沉浸于全球资本主义和跨国自由主义的不确定性戏剧。起初看似小规模冲突的事，或许仍能决定历史。既然我们不知道事情会如何发展，就值得关注涌现——以及紧急——的状态。希望与绝望在此挤在一起，有时依赖同样的技术。紧迫性在毁坏的地景中涌现；乌托邦梦想和粗鄙野心得以形成。在这场风暴中，全球化理论那些有保证的未来显得陌生而遥远。

Here, indeed, I write in conversation with other scholars who would interrupt the easy flow of global capital by conjuring a heady mixture of outrage and millenialism. In the interplay of ruin and possibility, they argue, lie alternative and more open forms of global commitment. Thinking through Indonesia’s history of anti-colonial struggle and state-sponsored terror, philosopher Pheng Cheah tells of radical nationalisms that offer populist hope at the same time as they are made possible by state disciplines (2003). Life and death haunt each other in these nationalisms, he says, making them both poison and medicine. Even the most utopian initiatives—say, human rights for women of the global south—are contaminated by the logics of power, and, yet, too, they carry our dreams for justice (Cheah 1997).

确实，我在这里与其他学者对话，他们通过召唤愤怒与千禧年主义的醉人混合，来打断全球资本的顺畅流动。他们认为，在毁灭与可能性的相互作用中，存在另类且更开放的全球承诺形式。哲学家 Pheng Cheah 思考印尼反殖民斗争和国家赞助的恐怖史，讲述了激进民族主义既提供民粹主义希望，又由国家规训使其成为可能（2003）。他说，在这些民族主义中，生与死相互萦绕，使它们既是毒药也是药物。即使最乌托邦的倡议——比如全球南方女性的人权——也受到权力逻辑的污染，然而它们也承载着我们关于正义的梦想（Cheah 1997）。

If justice and repression must be grasped simultaneously, so too must exploitation and creative labor. Thus, literary scholar Neferti Tadiar (forthcoming) introduces the concept of “historical experience” to tell of the subjective labor of the marginalized and displaced, which fuels narratives of capital and nation yet falls beyond these narratives’ scope of explanation. For example, the experience of Filipina labor migrants—maids, prostitutes, entertainers, all disgorged from the country to earn remittances—articulates and transforms the Philippines’ global disadvantage into both the worst disappointments and the most heartfelt desires. Their experience exposes them to the worst terrors of the global economy, even as it articulates the possibilities of new, emergent forms of social relation. This mingling of despair and hope reformulates representations of global capital, remaking the culture and politics of globalization.

如果正义与压迫必须同时把握，剥削与创造性劳动也必须同时把握。因此，文学学者内费尔蒂·塔迪亚尔（Neferti Tadiar，即将出版）引入“历史经验”概念，讲述边缘化和流离失所者的主体性劳动，这种劳动为资本与民族国家的叙事提供燃料，却落在这些叙事的解释范围之外。例如，菲律宾女性劳工移民——女佣、妓女、艺人，全都从国内被推向海外，以赚取侨汇——的经验，把菲律宾的全球劣势表述并转化为最深的失望和最真挚的欲望。她们的经验使她们暴露于全球经济最可怕的恐怖，同时也表述了新生的社会关系形式的可能性。这种绝望与希望的混合重新表述全球资本的再现，重塑全球化的文化与政治。
The most exciting feature of this conversation for me is its requirement that the analysis be located

the world of globalization’s struggles and passions. Unlike most social scientists and area studies specialists, these scholars refuse to objectify the participants from the perspective of an imagined global management. Instead, Cheah and Tadiar bring us to understand the risks, collusions, and uncertainties from the perspective of those whose well-being is at stake. This opens up the analysis to the promises and dangers of history; contingency matters because it shifts the options for justice and repression, exploitation and creative hope. In this same spirit, this book has followed the contending forms of hazard, curiosity, and zeal of natural resource entrepreneurs, environmental advocates, student nature lovers, and indigenous farmer-foragers.
对我来说，这场对话最令人兴奋的特征，是它要求把分析置于全球化斗争与激情的世界
。与大多数社会科学家和区域研究专家不同，这些学者拒绝从想象性的全球管理视角把参与者对象化。相反，Cheah 和 Tadiar 让我们从那些福祉受到威胁者的视角理解风险、共谋和不确定性。这使分析向历史的承诺与危险敞开；偶然性重要，因为它改变了正义与压迫、剥削与创造性希望的选择。本着同样的精神，本书追随自然资源企业家、环保倡导者、学生自然爱好者和原住民农耕—采集者相互竞争的冒险、好奇与热忱形式。

This perspective of engagement also informs Cheah’s argument for the importance of claims to the universal (2001). As long as area studies closes itself to the universal, he says, it will cordon off those it studies from participation in remaking the world. Only because area studies scholars have conventionally imagined themselves in the service of the all-seeing West, he argues, have they confined the scope of the non-Western dreams and nightmares they study into area-bound particularities. From inside any “area,” universal claims are key to global agency. Inspired by Cheah’s challenge, I have taken a close look at the universal, making it a key category for my research. I call universals “engaged” to acknowledge the fact that to be effective they must enter the fray. Universal claims allow people to make history, but not under the conditions those claims might lead them to choose.

这种介入的视角也影响了 Cheah 关于普遍性主张重要性的论证（2001）。他说，只要区域研究对普遍物封闭自己，它就会把它所研究的对象圈起来，不让其参与世界的重造。他论证说，只是因为区域研究学者习惯上把自己想象为服务于全视的西方，他们才把所研究的非西方梦想与噩梦的范围限定为区域性的特殊性。在任何“区域”内部，普遍性主张都是全球能动性的关键。受 Cheah 挑战的启发，我仔细审视普遍物，使其成为研究的关键范畴。我把这些普遍性称为“介入性的”，以承认这样一个事实：要有效，它们必须进入战斗。普遍性主张让人们能够创造历史，但不是在他们可能因这些主张而选择的条件下。

This book has argued that we know and use nature through engaged universals. The “environment” spreads around the world through the friction of engagement, both for commercial users, who tap into its divergences for capitalist commodity chains, and for advocates, who find in these same divergences the means to study, enjoy, or preserve it. As I have shown, what seem at first to be equivalent requirements to work across difference lead to contrasting consequences for humans and nonhumans. In the spirit of scholars such as Cheah and Tadiar, I suggest that social analysis can explore these diverging scenes of possibility only through its own engaged immersion in the histories it plots.

本书论证我们通过介入性的普遍性来认识和使用自然。“环境”通过介入的摩擦传遍世界，无论是对商业使用者——他们利用其分歧为资本主义商品链服务——还是对倡导者——他们在同样的分歧中找到研究、欣赏或保护它的手段。如我所展示的，起初看似同等的要求——跨越差异工作——对人类和非人类导致截然不同的后果。本着 Cheah 和 Tadiar 等学者的精神，我提出，社会分析只有通过自身对所描绘历史的介入性沉浸，才能探索这些分歧的可能性场景。

My own ability to enter this history is that of an ethnographer—a listener and a teller of tales. Yet my project stretches and changes the practice of ethnography. As I reach to describe global connections, my ethnography necessarily diverges from the holism of more familiar models, in which each anecdote or custom forms a scrap in a larger, unified pattern. Instead, following the example of subaltern studies historians who retrieve forgotten pasts plowed over by national histories, I endorse the fragment (Pandey 2000). In this project, I have used ethnographic fragments to interrupt stories of a unified and successful regime of global self-management.

我自己进入这段历史的能力，是民族志学者的能力——一个倾听者和讲故事者。然而我的项目延伸并改变了民族志实践。当我伸手描述全球联结时，我的民族志必然背离更熟悉模式的整体主义；在那些模式中，每则轶事或习俗都构成更大统一图案中的碎片。相反，我效仿那些打捞被国家历史碾过、遭到遗忘的过去的庶民研究历史学家，认可碎片（Pandey 2000）。在这个项目中，我用民族志碎片打断统一而成功的全球自我管理体制的故事。

Ethnographic fragments ask us to pay attention to details. The travels that inspire global connection turn out to be less controllable than those at the top imply. Making claims about scale, including globalization, turns out to be an arena of contention.
民族志碎片要求我们注意细节。激发全球联结的旅行，结果比高层所暗示的更不可控。关于尺度——包括全球化——的主张，结果是一个争论的竞技场。

And thus there is no reason to begin a retelling of global connections in imagined world centers such as New York, Tokyo, or Geneva. Globalization is not delivered whole and round like a pizza, to be munched and dismantled by the hungry margins. Global connections are made in fragments—although some fragments are more powerful than others. My telling of global connections has featured rural Kalimantan, where the fragmentary nature of global process is especially evident. Following global connections out of Kalimantan, I found myself exploring other sites, including powerful centers of finance, science, and policy. But these, too, produce only fragments, and my Kalimantan beginnings remind me of this. Some fragments are able to make themselves look whole. Honoring the fragment means acknowledging this power but not accepting it as a done deal. Through fragments, ethnographers can immerse themselves in the contests and engagements of the present.

因此，没有理由从纽约、东京或日内瓦等想象的世界中心开始重述全球联结。全球化不是像披萨一样整块完整地送达，供饥饿的边缘啃食和拆解。全球联结是在碎片中制造的——尽管有些碎片比其他碎片更强大。我对全球联结的讲述以加里曼丹乡村为特色，在那里全球过程的碎片性尤为明显。顺着全球联结走出加里曼丹，我发现自己探索其他地点，包括金融、科学和政策的强大中心。但这些地方也只生产碎片，我在加里曼丹的开端提醒我这一点。有些碎片能够使自己看起来完整。尊重碎片意味着承认这种权力，但不把它当作既成事实接受。通过碎片，民族志学者可以沉浸于当下的争夺与介入。

Fragments need not reduce analysis to simply noticing idiosyncrasy and happenstance. This book has proposed a series of methods to enable more nuanced understandings of global connection. They interrupt dominant stories of globalization to offer more realistic alternatives. Instead of positing a triumphant global regime, these methods guide us to the disjunctions of global travel, such as those I have traced in the excesses of capitalist proliferations and the awkward conjunctures of social movement building. Here it is possible to consider the practical shape of global politics and culture without the interference of self-fulfilling prophecies.
碎片不必把分析降低为仅仅注意到特异性和偶然。本书提出了一系列方法，以便对全球联结作出更细致的理解。它们打断全球化的主导故事，提供更现实的替代方案。这些方法不是设定一个胜利的全球体制，而是引导我们走向全球旅行的断裂，例如我在资本主义增殖的过度和社会运动建设的别扭汇合中所追踪的那些。在这里，可以考虑全球政治与文化的实际形态，而不受自我实现预言的干扰。

Instead of requiring an evolutionary process of change, these methods show the pervasive effects of historical encounters. Instead of starting with the dichotomy between global force and local response, these methods show the importance of contingent and botched encounters in shaping both business-as-usual and its radical refusals. Thus, I have described how cosmopolitan nature loving—like capitalist resource use—has emerged in the crossroads of old cultural legacies. I show how well-intentioned advocacy for the indigenous peoples of the forest extends the logics of power, forging new gaps in what can be said about people and forests. Yet sometimes in the urgency of a campaign, such misunderstandings are productive as objects in common begin to coalesce in the space of partial agreement. It is these moments of conjuncture that make social activism worthwhile. Meanwhile, they interrupt and change the principles of activism, introducing further genealogies of meaning and coercion into the risky mix that signifies empowerment.

这些方法不要求一个进化的变化过程，而是展示历史遭遇的普遍效果。这些方法不从全球力量与地方回应之间的二分开始，而是展示偶然与搞砸的遭遇在塑造一切照常及其激进拒绝中的重要性。因此，我描述了世界主义自然之爱——像资本主义资源利用一样——如何在旧文化遗产的十字路口出现。我展示了对森林原住民善意倡导如何延伸权力逻辑，在人与森林的可言说范围中制造新的空白。然而，有时在运动的紧迫情势中，这类误解具有生产力，因为共同对象开始在部分共识的空间中凝聚。正是这些汇合时刻使社会行动主义值得付出。同时，它们打断并改变行动主义的原则，把更多意义与强制的谱系引入标志着赋权的风险混合体。

Such fragments of varied schemes and travels and encounters do create a world of global connections. These are global connections made, and muddled, in friction. Curiosity about such friction might yet re-open the mystery of our times.
这些多样方案、旅行和遭遇的碎片确实创造了一个全球联结的世界。这些全球联结是在摩擦中制造、也被摩擦搅乱的。对这种摩擦的好奇，或许仍能重新打开我们时代的神秘。
